subsystems.name: Artificial muscle element
subsystems.role: the part that contracts or expands when stimulated, mimicking biological muscle.
parts: dielectric elastomer film or ionic polymer membrane

subsystems.name: Compliant electrodes
subsystems.role: carry charge across the muscle without cracking as it stretches.

subsystems.name: Neuromorphic controller
subsystems.role: generates muscle commands as timed spikes, the way motor neurons do.

subsystems.name: Embedded sensing
subsystems.role: gives the controller feedback on length, force and temperature.

subsystems.name: Drive electronics
subsystems.role: converts low-voltage control signals into the higher voltages some artificial muscles need.

subsystems.name: Mechanical integration
subsystems.role: packages muscles into a working limb or joint.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the elastomer
buildSteps.detail: Silicone or acrylic precursors are mixed and cast into thin films a few tens of micrometres thick, then cured.

buildSteps.title: Apply compliant electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Conductive layers are printed or sprayed onto both faces so they can stretch with the film without losing contact.

buildSteps.title: Stack and laminate
buildSteps.detail: Many thin muscle layers are bonded together with insulating interlayers to multiply force while keeping voltage manageable.

buildSteps.title: Embed sensors
buildSteps.detail: Stretchable strain and force sensors are laminated into the stack and wired out.

buildSteps.title: Design the neuromorphic controller
buildSteps.detail: A spiking neural network is trained in simulation to map desired motion to spike patterns that drive the muscles.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the control chip
buildSteps.detail: The network is mapped onto neuromorphic hardware, where neurons and synapses are physical circuits rather than software.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the actuator module
buildSteps.detail: Muscle stack, sensors, drive electronics and chip are integrated into a sealed unit with tendons or linkages.

buildSteps.title: Test and iterate
buildSteps.detail: The module is cycled millions of times to measure force, speed, efficiency and wear, and the controller is retuned.

prerequisites.tech: Electroactive polymers with high strain and long life
prerequisites.why: lab devices achieve large movement but often need high voltage and fatigue quickly.
research chips exist, but none are yet built to drive high-power actuators in real time.
sensors and wiring must survive the same stretching as the muscle.
artificial muscles are nonlinear and hard to control with conventional methods.
many artificial muscles need hundreds to thousands of volts, which is bulky to supply.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations of single artificial-muscle actuators and spiking control of simple soft robots
pathway.unlocks: proof that spike-timed control can drive muscle-like motion.

pathway.milestone: integrated muscle modules with embedded neuromorphic chips tested in grippers or robotic limbs
pathway.unlocks: closed-loop control at the component level.

pathway.milestone: humanoid-scale limbs combining many muscle modules with learned spiking controllers
pathway.unlocks: robots that move with biological smoothness and efficiency.

pathway.milestone: commercial prosthetics or humanoid platforms using muscle-like actuation
pathway.unlocks: lightweight, quiet, compliant machines for homes and workplaces.
